title: 5.0L Accessory Drive — Component Location
introduction:
For the 5.0L 32V Ti-VCT engine, I start with the large crankshaft pulley near the bottom of the drawing and follow the highlighted belt paths around the accessories. Think of it as a road map for engine rotation: a crossing in the perspective drawing is a reason to follow the line carefully, rather than jump to another path.

Match each callout to its adjacent table entry. The drawing distinguishes the accessory drive belt from the A/C compressor belt, and the idler pulley assembly from the accessory drive belt tensioner. The tensioner maintains belt tension; an idler guides the belt. The coolant pump and generator pulleys pass rotation into their respective assemblies, while the compressor pulley belongs to the air-conditioning drive.

This reference helps identify the visible drive components and understand their relationships. It does not give belt-release direction, installation order, tool sizes, tightening values or inspection limits. Use the matching engine-specific service procedure before removing or installing a belt.
